title: Infer a request's rung from BRIEF.md and addenda, not a word list
summary: Planning gives nearly every request the Implementation rung because `infer_rung` in reading.rs treats any touched path, `change` capability or word like "code" or "ci" as proof, so age alone orders the queue. The goal is for the rung to come from the BRIEF.md requirement or owner addendum a request serves, so the 2026-10-16 speed items (s6tr, q0xy) rank above older plain implementation work. The audience is the owner, who reads the plan order.

defaults_applied.how: New and updated tests; cargo test and clippy are acceptance criteria.
The fix replaces the word-list heuristic itself, not just the ordering of the two items.
Criteria assert the rung and order for the speed requests, not that code exists.
Behavior criteria are checkable with cargo test.
Doc comments and the decision entry are written for an outside reader.
One focused change to rung inference.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Fix site is `infer_rung` and `plan_entry` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs; plan.rs sorts by (rung, age) and stays as is.

A request that serves a BRIEF.md addendum or requirement (for example the 2026-10-16 speed addendum) ranks at BriefRequirements, above Implementation. Roles still cannot change the top two rungs; this only affects ordering.

Deterministic matching: the request text and reading summary are matched against BRIEF.md section headings and addenda text, passed in through the Lookup struct so plan_entry stays free of I/O. No model call is added.

The IMPLEMENTATION_WORDS list stops being sufficient evidence on its own. A request that matches no brief section falls back to Implementation only when a path is touched or the reading chose `change`, else None, as today.
The ordering rule in the plan.rs docs stays: rung first, then oldest first.
BRIEF.md is protected and is not edited.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs plans a request about CI routing or parallel jobs against the real 2026-10-16 speed addendum text and asserts its rung is above Implementation. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

A unit test builds a plan from an old plain implementation request (a typo fix) and a newer speed-addendum request, and asserts the speed request is ordered first. Run `cargo test -p athena-core plan`.

A request that matches no brief section and has only an IMPLEMENTATION_WORDS word, such as 'fix a bug', no longer gets a rung from the word alone. A test asserts this, and the existing test `a_rung_is_inferred_from_evidence_or_flagged_never_defaulted_to_implementation` is updated to match.
`cargo test` passes and `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean across the workspace.

The doc comments on `IMPLEMENTATION_WORDS`, `infer_rung` and the plan.rs module header say the rung comes from what a request serves in BRIEF.md and its addenda. A short entry in docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md records the call and the alternatives (a model-chosen rung, keeping the word list).

out_of_scope: Re-planning or reordering the 30 items of #116 (a later run of the fixed planner does that).
Changing the ladder's rungs or which roles may change them.
Changing the CI routing or parallel jobs work itself (s6tr, q0xy).
departures: Cost and time sit slightly above the reference. The change touches inference logic that existing tests pin, so several tests must be rewritten.
